questions.q: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2: 3: 7 and the radius of the circumscribed ircle is $10 \mathrm{cm}$. The length of the smallest ide is
questions.solution: Given, that angles of a triangles are $2 x, 3 x$ and $7 x$ Since, $2 x+3 x+7 x=180\Rightarrow 12 x=180^{{}^{\circ}} \Rightarrow x=15^{{}^{\circ}}$ So, angles are $30^{{}^{\circ}}, 45^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $105^{{}^{\circ}}$ Now, $\frac{a}{\sin 30^{{}^{\circ}}}=2 R\Rightarrow \quad \frac{a}{\frac{1}{2}}=2 \times 10 \quad[\because R=10 \mathrm{cm}]\Rightarrow \quad 2 a=20 \Rightarrow a=10 \mathrm{cm}$

questions.q: If in a $\triangle A B C, A D, B E$ and $C F$ are the altitudes and $R$ is the circumradius, then the radius of the circumcircle of $\Delta D E F$ is
questions.solution: Let circumradius of $\Delta$ DEF be $R'$ We know. $\angle F D E=180^{{}^{\circ}}-2 A$ and $F E=R \sin 2 A$ Now, by sine rule in $\triangle D E F2 R^{\prime}=\frac{E F}{\sin \angle F D E}=\frac{A \sin 2 A}{\sin \left(180^{{}^{\circ}}-2 A\right)}\thereforeR^{\prime}=\frac{R}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In $\Delta A B C$, if $a^{2} \cos ^{2} A-b^{2}-c^{2}=0,$ then
questions.solution: We have, $a^{2} \cos ^{2} A-b^{2}-c^{2}=0\Rightarrow \quad a^{2} \cos ^{2} A=b^{2}+c^{2}$ Also in $\triangle A B C$, we have $\begin{aligned} \cos A=\frac{b^{2}+c^{2}-a^{2}}{2 b c} &=\frac{a^{2} \cos ^{2} A-a^{2}}{2 b c} \\=& \frac{-a^{2}\left(1-\cos ^{2} A\right)}{2 b c}=\frac{-a^{2} \sin ^{2} A}{2 b c} < 0 \\ & \quad \because 0 < A < \pi, a, b, c > 0 \end{aligned}\Rightarrow \cos A < 0 \Rightarrow A$ lies in IInd quadrant. $\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\pi}{2} < A < \pi$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a $\triangle A B C, a, b, c$ are the sides of the triangle opposite to the angles $A, B, C,$ respectively. Then, the value of $a^{3} \sin (B-C)+b^{3} \sin (C-A)+c^{3} \sin (A-B)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\sum a^{3} \sin (B-C)$
$=\sum k^{3} \sin ^{3} A \sin (B-C)$
$$
\begin{aligned}\left[\because \frac{a}{\sin A}=\frac{b}{\sin B}=\frac{c}{\sin C}=k\right] \\=\sum k^{3}\left[\sin ^{2} A \sin (B+C) \sin (B-C)\right] \\=k^{3}\left[\left\{\sin ^{2} A \times \frac{1}{2}(\cos 2 C-\cos 2 B)\right\}\right.\\+\sin ^{2} B \times \frac{1}{2}(\cos 2 A-\cos 2 C) \\\left.+\sin ^{2} C \times \frac{1}{2}(\cos 2 B-\cos 2 A)\right] \end{aligned}
$$
$=\frac{k^{3}}{2}\left[\sin ^{2} A\left(1-2 \sin ^{2} C-1+2 \sin ^{2} B\right)\right.$
$+\sin ^{2} B\left(1-2 \sin ^{2} A-1+2 \sin ^{2} C\right)$
$\left.+\sin ^{2} C\left(1-2 \sin ^{2} B-1+2 \sin ^{2} A\right)\right]$
$=\frac{k^{3}}{2}\left[-2 \sin ^{2} A \sin ^{2} C+2 \sin ^{2} A \sin ^{2} B\right.$
$-2 \sin ^{2} B \sin ^{2} A+2 \sin ^{2} B \sin ^{2} C$
$\left.-2 \sin ^{2} C \sin ^{2} B+2 \sin ^{2} C \sin ^{2} A\right]$
$=\frac{k^{3}}{2}[0]=0$

questions.q: Lines $x+y=1$ and $3 y=x+3$ intersect the ellipse $x^{2}+9 y^{2}=9$ at the points $P, Q$ and $R$. The area of the $\triangle P Q R$ is
questions.solution: Given equation of ellipse x^{2}+9 y^{2}=9 $\Rightarrow \quad \frac{x^{2}}{9}+\frac{y^{2}}{1}=1$ and equation of lines x+y=1 $\text{ and }3 y=x+3 or $\quad $\frac{x}{(-3)}+\frac{y}{1}=1\therefore$ Area of $\Delta P Q R=\left|\begin{array}{c|ccc}0 & 1 & 1 \\ -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 9 / 5 & -4 / 5 & 1\end{array}\right| \mid=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{24}{5}+\frac{12}{5}\right]=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{36}{5}=\frac{18}{5}$

questions.q: Let $p, q$ and $r$ be the sides opposite to the angles $P, Q$ and $R,$ respectively in a $\Delta P Q R.$ If $r^{2} \sin P \sin Q=p q,$ then the triangle is
questions.solution: We know that in $\Delta A B C\frac{a}{\sin A}=\frac{b}{\sin B}=\frac{c}{\sin C}=2 R\therefore \quad r^{2} \sin P \sin Q=p q\Rightarrow r^{2} \cdot \frac{p}{2 R_{1}} \cdot \frac{q}{2 R_{1}}=p q,$ where $R_{1}$ is circumras of $\Delta P Q R$. $\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow$& r^{2}=4 R_{1}^{2} \\ \Rightarrow & r=2 R_{1} \\ \Rightarrow & 2 R_{1} \sin R=2 R_{1}\end{array}\Rightarrow \quad R_{1}=90^{{}^{\circ}}\therefore \Delta P Q R$ is right angled.$

questions.q: Let $p, q$ and $r$ be the side4s opposite to the angles $P, Q$ and $R,$ respectively in a $\Delta P Q R$. Then, $2 p r \sin  \left(\frac{p-Q+R}{2}\right)equals$
questions.solution: In $\Delta P Q R, P+Q+R=180^{{}^{\circ}}\begin{aligned} \therefore 2 p r \sin \left(\frac{P-Q+R}{2}\right) &=2 p r \sin \frac{180^{{}^{\circ}}-Q-Q}{2} \\ &=2 p r \sin \left(90^{{}^{\circ}}-Q\right) \\ &=2 p r \cos Q \\=&\left(\quad \ln \Delta P Q R \cos Q=\frac{p^{2}+r^{2}-q^{2}}{2 p r}\right) \\=& 2 p r\left(\frac{p^{2}+r^{2}-q^{2}}{2 p r}\right)=p^{2}+r^{2}-q^{2} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $p, q$ and $r$ be the altitudes of a triangle with area $S$ and perimeter $2 t .$ Then, the value of $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}+\frac{1}{r}$ is
questions.solution: According to question, $S=\frac{1}{2} a \cdot p$ $\begin{array}{c} =\frac{1}{2}$ b $\cdot$ q=$\frac{1}{2}$ c $\cdot$ r \\ \therefore \quad $\frac{1}{p}=\frac{a}{2 S}, \frac{1}{q}=\frac{b}{2 S}, \frac{1}{r}=\frac{c}{2 S}$\\ \therefore \quad $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}+\frac{1}{r}=\frac{1}{2 S}($ a+b+c)=$\frac{2 t}{2 S}=\frac{t}{S} \end{array}$
